summary.name: Safari
summary.one_liner: Apple's built-in web browser for Mac, emphasizing privacy protections, extension support and battery life.
use_cases: browse the web privately on a Mac
check which trackers are blocked on a site
use browser extensions with low battery drain
summary.what_it_does: Safari is Apple's native web browser for Macs. It includes Intelligent Tracking Prevention, which identifies cross-site trackers and helps stop them from profiling or following users across websites. Private Browsing adds further protections, such as locking windows when not in use and removing unique trackers from URLs. The Privacy Report button in the Safari menu shows trackers prevented on the current site, and a weekly Privacy Report shows protection over time. The page also includes a feature table claiming Safari blocks third-party cookies by default and hides IP addresses from known trackers, while Chrome does not.
notable: Intelligent Tracking Prevention with machine-learning tracker detection
Weekly Privacy Report and per-site tracker snapshot
Private Browsing removes unique trackers from URLs
Supports third-party extensions and claims industry-leading battery life
caveats: Feature comparison with Chrome is provided by Apple's own page and is not independently verified
Page describes Safari for Macs; no other platforms are named in the page text
